state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, the operation is a horizontal translation. Remember that \( f(x - a) \) actually translates the function to the right by \( a \) units, not up.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, okay! So, if \( f(x - a) \) translates the graph to the right by \( a \) units, does that mean for \( f(x - 3) \), it actually moves the graph to the right by 3 units? I thought it was going up because of the way the numbers looked. Can you explain why it goes right instead of up?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, \( f(x - 3) \) actually translates the graph to the right by 3 units because of the way the function is structured. It may seem like it goes up due to the numbers, but it is a horizontal translation.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher correctly identifies the misconception and provides accurate mathematics, but simply repeats procedural rules without explanation, fails to engage the student's explicit request for understanding ('Can you explain why it goes right instead of up?'), and the student shows no evidence of improved reasoning by the end.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently states explicit procedures (identifying the operation and applying the rule), directly corrects the procedural error (wrong direction and axis), and provides the specific rule for horizontal translations, which is textbook rule-based instruction.
